Landed cost is the full price of an imported good by the time it reaches your warehouse: the goods, freight and insurance, customs duty, IGST, port and clearance charges and transport. Divide it by the number of units to get the true cost per unit.
Is IGST part of my landed cost?
IGST is paid at import, but a registered business can usually claim it back as input tax credit. The wizard shows the cost both ways. Tick the box if you claim the credit and it shows the net cost.
Why does the freight box say 20 percent?

When freight is not known, customs adds 20 percent of the FOB value as freight and 1.125 percent as insurance to work out the assessable value. If you know your real freight and insurance, enter them and the duty becomes more accurate.
Which charges should I put in step 2?

Terminal handling, the shipping line delivery order, CFS or ICD charges, your customs broker fee, transport to your warehouse and anything else you pay, such as testing or inspection. Your forwarder and broker can give you these figures before the ship arrives.
